proposals.evidence: The Harvest phase appends to breath_log.json with an unsafe truncating-open write (json.dump(open(path,'w'), ...)). This opens the file in 'w' mode (truncating it to zero bytes) BEFORE serialization runs; if serialization then raises, the file is left truncated and any uncommitted entries are lost irrecoverably. The same root failure mode -- 'the breath_log write step is not crash-safe' -- has now bitten three times: (a) 2026-04-30 (breath discoveries[4]) first named the hazard explicitly ('A failed write while the file is open truncates it - always read fully into memory before opening for write') as a near-miss after a surrogate-pair encode error; (b) 2026-05-13 DATA LOSS INCIDENT lost 4 uncommitted entries (2026-05-05/06/09/12) via ensure_ascii=False on a string containing UTF-8 surrogate chars; (c) 2026-06-06 DATA LOSS INCIDENT clobbered the uncommitted log mid-breath via json.dump(open('w')), forcing reconstruction of the 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-05 entries. Two actual irreversible-data-loss incidents plus one prior documented near-miss of the identical root cause. The proximate triggers differ (ensure_ascii surrogate vs truncating-open) but the failure outcome and the fix are identical.
proposals.proposed_change: Add an explicit crash-safe-write rule to the Harvest section of SKILL.md: NEVER write breath_log.json (or improvement_trajectory.json) with json.dump(open(path,'w'), ...). Instead: (1) read the full existing file into memory first; (2) serialize the updated object to a string with json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=True) so any encoding error raises BEFORE the file is touched; (3) write the string to a temp file in the same directory and os.replace() it over the target (atomic). This guarantees the on-disk file is never left truncated even if serialization or the process fails mid-write.
proposals.expected_improvement: Eliminates the recurring breath_log/trajectory truncation-and-data-loss class entirely. Would have prevented both the 2026-05-13 loss (4 entries) and the 2026-06-06 loss (2 entries) and the reconstruction labor each required. The atomic temp-file-then-replace pattern is a one-time ~10-line change and makes every future Harvest write durable.

NEW LIVE OCCURRENCE, and the first one to bite the SECOND file prop-004 explicitly names (improvement_trajectory.json), not breath_log.json. This morning's Harvest used exactly the anti-pattern prop-004 forbids: json.dump(d, open('doc/reports/improvement_trajectory.json','w',encoding='utf-8'), ...). The dump raised UnicodeEncodeError mid-write ('utf-8' codec can't encode '���', a stray surrogate carried in PRE-EXISTING data from a prior write), AFTER 'w' had already truncated the file. Reload failed with JSONDecodeError (line 307) — the file was left half-written. Recovery cost: git checkout -- improvement_trajectory.json, then a re-do with the crash-safe recipe (json.dumps to string + .encode('utf-8','replace') to scrub surrogates + single write). This is direct field confirmation of prop-004's failure mode on a real run. Two refinements for the applied fix: (1) the proposed ensure_ascii=True would have PREVENTED this (surrogates ascii-escape cleanly instead of raising on utf-8 encode) — concrete proof ensure_ascii=True is the right serialization guard; (2) add a surrogate-scrub (.encode('utf-8','replace').decode()) because corrupt surrogates can ALREADY be resident in these files from past bad writes, so even a safe new write must sanitize inherited data. RECOMMENDATION: apply prop-004 now; the hazard is no longer hypothetical for trajectory file too.

proposals.evidence: A recurring class of failure: when a grid/registry convention is introduced or changed, a downstream scorer/listener tool keeps applying the OLD parsing rule and silently undercounts, and subsequent breaths then encode the depressed reading as a structural fact (a 'wall'), foreclosing real work for weeks. Four occurrences of the same root pattern -- a downstream tool out of sync with a runtime convention: (a) 2026-04-14 registry files with _comment_ string-valued keys caused sequence_pipeline_scorer to silently skip the entire file; (b) 2026-04-22 PascalCase .gd filenames (NeuralNetworks_VR.gd) produced garden_listener cache keys that did not match snake_case map lookups, hiding 25+ already-voiced ML artifacts; (c) 2026-05-28 the '#'-prefix cell-comment sigil (added by grid commit c679a7b4c) was parsed by the scorer as an empty token, holding primitives stage_3 at 98% and pinning the FOCUS_VECTOR primary at HEAD 3; (d) 2026-06-11 the delegate_to + map_ready promotion convention (dna_*/loom_*/mill_*/vector *_xl) was ignored by load_all_registry_scenes (it recorded only literal-scene artifacts), undercounting 4 forces + 19 color interactables and depressing forces to HEAD 3 and color to HEAD 2 -- while the prior FIVE breaths (2026-05-30 onward) declared the entire spine saturated at HEAD>=6 with only voicing/captures left. GridInteractablesComponent.gd:387 resolved all of these correctly at runtime; the scorer did not. The compounding harm is not the tool bug alone but that breaths trusted the depressed count as truth.
proposals.proposed_change: Add a 'convention-drift cross-check' to the Read/Evaluate phase. (1) Before concluding a sequence's HEAD/gap is real, resolve its unresolved interactable tokens against the RUNTIME resolver (GridInteractablesComponent.gd's delegate_to + registry-key lookup) rather than trusting the scorer's literal-scene count -- especially when a single sequence lags the spine modal HEAD or sits at a near-threshold percentage (artifacts/docs 90-99%). (2) When a grid/registry convention is introduced or changed (new cell sigil, new delegate/promotion key, filename-case rule), treat it as triggering a tracked sweep of the seven downstream tools (pipeline scorer, pathfinder, garden listener, release gates, capture pipeline, sequence verifier, map studio); a convention honored by the runtime but not by a scorer WILL silently diverge. (3) Gate prop-003's wall-detection on this cross-check: never auto-retarget the success metric off pipeline-HEAD on the basis of a 'spine saturated at HEAD>=6' reading until the lagging-sequence convention cross-check has passed.

proposals.proposed_change: Add a 'recent-commit regression re-scan' to the Read phase of SKILL.md, run BEFORE trusting any prior-breath saturation/HEAD reading. (1) List maps touched since the last breath: git log --since='<last_breath_timestamp>' --name-only (or diff HEAD against the last breath's recorded commit) filtered to commons/maps/*/map_data.json. (2) For each newly-declared or modified map, confirm BOTH blurb.md and intent.md exist under commons/maps/<MapName>/. (3) Any map missing its doc pair is an immediate documentation-stage HEAD regression for its sequence and is the cheapest available pipeline-advance work — prioritize it over voicing/captures. (4) Project-discipline note (already surfaced verbatim in 2026-06-14 and 2026-06-15 breath discoveries): a map should be committed in the SAME commit as its blurb/intent; the breather should treat a bare feat(map) commit as a regression signal. This is the concrete per-sequence guard that pairs with prop-005's runtime-resolver convention cross-check and supplies the content-regression half of prop-003's wall-detection trigger gate.
proposals.expected_improvement: Converts ~1 breath-of-rediscovery per regression into a single cheap Read-phase check; surfaces a doc regression the same day the map lands rather than 1-2 breaths later; and hardens prop-003's 'spine saturated at HEAD>=6' auto-retarget trigger against the content-regression failure mode (prop-005 only guards the scorer-drift mode).
